strings.name: Richard Stallman
strings.summary: Richard Stallman launched GNU and the free-software movement, advocating users' freedom to run, study, modify and share software. He developed tools including GNU Emacs and the GNU compiler, founded the Free Software Foundation and used copyleft licensing to preserve redistribution rights. His technical and ethical advocacy influenced software communities, while controversial public remarks led to his 2019 resignation and opposition to his 2021 return to the foundation's board.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2021. This is not a daily news archive. Shared achievements are credited to collaborators and teams.
strings.influence.rationale: Launched GNU and the free-software movement, advancing institutional debates about software freedom, open licensing and developer collaboration.

strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Harvard physics bachelor's (1974); graduate study at MIT
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: GNU and free software
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Established GNU and developed foundational free-software editors, compilers and debugging tools.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Copyleft licensing
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Promoted copyright licenses that preserve users' freedom to copy, modify and redistribute software.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Returned to FSF board
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Announced his return to the board, drawing public opposition from organizations including FSFE.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Resigned from FSF leadership
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Resigned as president and board member amid controversy over his remarks.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: MacArthur and Hopper awards
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Received a MacArthur Fellowship and ACM's Grace Murray Hopper Award for software work.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: First GNU GPL
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Version1 of the GNU General Public License expressed redistribution conditions in a general software license.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Founded the FSF
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Established the nonprofit foundation to support GNU and the free-software movement.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Began full-time GNU development
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Left MIT employment to implement the previously announced free operating-system project.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Announced GNU
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Proposed a Unix-like operating system composed of free software.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Developed Emacs
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Developed the extensible editor at MIT's AI laboratory.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Physics bachelor's degree
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Graduated from Harvard, then studied physics at MIT while continuing software work.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in New York
